title: IDEAlign: Comparing Ideas of Large Language Models to Domain Expert
abstract: arXiv:2509.02855v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to produce open-ended, interpretive annotations, yet there is no validated, scalable measure of idea-level similarity to expert annotations. We (i) introduce the content evaluation of LLM annotations as a core, understudied task, (ii) propose IDEAlign for capturing expert similarity judgments via pick-the-odd-one-out tasks, and (iii) benchmark various similarity methods (text embeddings, topic models, and LLM-as-a-judge) against these human ratings. Applying this approach to two real-world educational datasets (e.g., interpreting math reasoning and feedback generation), we find that most metrics fail to capture the nuanced dimensions of similarity meaningful to experts. LLM-as-a-judge performs best (11~18% improvement over other methods) but still falls short of expert alignment, making it useful as a triage tool rather than a substitute for human review. translated_title: IDEAlign：比较大型语言模型的想法与领域专家
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于生成开放式、解释性的注释，但目前缺乏经过验证的、可扩展的衡量注释与专家注释在想法层面相似性的指标。我们（i）将LLM注释的内容评估引入为核心但研究不足的任务，（ii）提出IDEAlign方法，通过“选出异类”任务捕捉专家的相似性判断，以及（iii）将各种相似性方法（文本嵌入、主题模型和LLM作为评判者）与这些人类评分进行基准测试。将该方法应用于两个真实世界的教育数据集（例如，解释数学推理和反馈生成），我们发现大多数指标无法捕捉对专家有意义且微妙的相似性维度。LLM作为评判者的表现最佳（比其他方法提高11~18%），但仍未达到专家对齐水平，因此更适合作为分诊工具，而非人类审查的替代品。我们的工作展示了这一任务的难度，并强调了进一步发展的必要性。
tldr: 本文提出IDEAlign方法，通过“选出异类”任务评估LLM注释与专家想法的相似性，发现现有指标大多失效，LLM作为评判者虽最优但仍需人类审查辅助。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces IDEAlign to evaluate idea-level similarity between LLM annotations and expert judgments via odd-one-out tasks, finding most metrics fail and LLM-as-a-judge, though best, still requires human review.
